Verdict as recorded: Unknown — trial postponed to September 1974; individual disposition not located

Charges as recorded: Murder and rioting — one of the eleven Atmore-Holman Brothers indicted over the January 18, 1974 Atmore prison rebellion

updates.charges: First-degree murder allegation arising from the March 1974 Holman Prison incident involving Tommy Dotson and a guard
updates.sentence: No sentence imposed in this prosecution. The Black Panther, March 8, 1975, printed page11, reports that the trial began February14,1975 and the judge directed a not-guilty verdict after contradictory prosecution testimony. The report identifies this charge as first-degree murder arising from a March1974 Holman Prison incident involving Tommy Dotson and a guard, distinct from the January18 uprising charges against other defendants. This disposition does not establish physical release from pre-existing imprisonment. Source: https://www.marxists.org/history/usa/pubs/black-panther/13%20no%203%201-28%20mar%208%201975.pdf#page=11

updates.sentence: No sentence imposed in this prosecution. The Black Panther, March 8, 1975, printed page11, reports that the judge dropped Ellis's charges for lack of evidence in February1975. Its summary gives February14 for both defendants while its detailed account places Ellis's trial the day after Paradise's; no exact individual disposition day is assigned here. The report identifies this charge as first-degree murder arising from a March1974 Holman Prison incident involving Tommy Dotson and a guard, distinct from the January18 uprising charges against other defendants. This disposition does not establish physical release from pre-existing imprisonment. Source: https://www.marxists.org/history/usa/pubs/black-panther/13%20no%203%201-28%20mar%208%201975.pdf#page=11
